short_definition: Interactive command-driven xBase/FoxPro-inspired runtime and documentation environment.
student_note: Program used to learn database concepts.
user_note: Command environment used to work with structured data.
developer_note: Runtime application and command surface layered over engine, HELP, metadata, and SelfDoc.

short_definition: Provenance and verification authority for documentation and metadata evidence.
student_note: The system that helps DotTalk++ check itself.
user_note: Verification system behind trustworthy manuals and HELP.
developer_note: Evidence/provenance subsystem that harvests, stages, validates, reports, and protects documentation truth.

short_definition: Import-safe long-text side table for SelfDoc metadata/diagram lanes.
developer_note: v1 long-text staging table for metadata/diagram work.

short_definition: A reviewed, canonical specification of a schema, interface, or behavior together with its declared proof/truth state; the authority a component is measured against.
student_note: A written and reviewed promise for how something must be shaped or behave.
user_note: The reviewed definition a feature is checked against.
developer_note: Reviewed spec (e.g. a .dtschema field contract, or an interface/behavior contract) carrying identity invariants and an explicit proof state; the registry and tests are DERIVED from it, so drift fails. Distinct from the physical DBF/code that implements it.
do_not_confuse_with: the physical schema/DBF that implements it; AIF claim

short_definition: The single security and user system: SYSUSER (authentication credential), SYSMEMBER (the principal/actor), and the RBAC catalogs, enforced by the acting-member and agent_permitted() gate.
student_note: The one place the program checks who you are and what you may do.
user_note: The single sign-in and permission system every feature uses.
developer_note: Canonical principal and RBAC system: SYSUSER credential plus SYSMEMBER actor plus SYSROLE/PERM/ROLEPERM/MEMROLE/OVERRIDE/ASSIGN/GRANT, gated by principal_key()/act_as/agent_permitted(). Every system references members by id or MKEY; there is no second user or credential store.
do_not_confuse_with: AIF lane ownership; free-text stewardship (selfdoc OWNER)

short_definition: WHO a command surface is for: user | developer | sample | internal. One of three orthogonal axes that the single status: field in @dottalk.usage currently conflates.
student_note: Tells you whether a command is meant for you or for someone working on the engine.
user_note: A developer-audience command is not broken; it is simply not aimed at you.
developer_note: PROPOSED 2026-09-02, awaiting owner ruling. Measured basis: 242 usage contracts declare 24 distinct status values. Eight of them answer WHO rather than HOW FINISHED -- developer(10), implementation-helper(3), sample-extension(2), dev-tool, dev-canary, backend-helper, supplemental, documentation-example.
legacy_terms: developer; dev-tool; dev-canary; sample-extension; backend-helper; supplemental; documentation-example; implementation-helper
do_not_confuse_with: completeness (how finished); lifecycle (whether it is going away)

short_definition: HOW FINISHED a command surface is: complete | in-progress | template | reference-only. Distinct from whether it runs, which is measured at runtime and never declared by hand.
student_note: in-progress means it works today and is still growing; it is not a promise that everything is there.
user_note: in-progress is NOT unsupported. It runs, it is actively developed, and it makes no claim of completeness.
developer_note: PROPOSED 2026-09-02, awaiting owner ruling. This axis is the one the current vocabulary cannot express, which is why supported-stub-mixed and supported-conditional exist -- someone needed two axes and had one field. Owner 2026-09-02 on SQL/SQLSEL: 'we are actively developing sql sqlsel, so it isn't unsupported, it's just not a claim of completeness' -> in-progress. Owner on TVISION: '.tvision is a working template not a stub' -> template, NOT stub.
legacy_terms: experimental; stub; supported-stub; supported-stub-mixed; supported-conditional; implementation-present; placeholder-shim
do_not_confuse_with: dispatchability (whether the command is registered and runs -- MEASURED, not declared); audience

short_definition: WHETHER A SURFACE IS GOING AWAY: current | deprecated | superseded.
student_note: A deprecated command still runs, but do not build on it.
user_note: Deprecated means it works now and will not always.
developer_note: PROPOSED 2026-09-02, awaiting owner ruling. LMDB_UTIL declares deprecated in its own contract and the manual published it as supported -- the most misleading row measured on 2026-09-02, because a reader cannot tell a command being retired from one being recommended.
do_not_confuse_with: completeness (an in-progress command is current, not deprecated)

short_definition: OVERLOADED, AND THAT IS THE PROBLEM. In the catalog it means the command is registered and dispatchable. In an @dottalk.usage contract it has been used to mean mature and complete. Two concepts, one word.
student_note: If a page says supported, ask supported in which sense.
user_note: The manual currently prints one word for two different questions.
developer_note: PROPOSED 2026-09-02, awaiting owner ruling. MEASURED: of 109 published commands that also declare a contract status, 33 disagree with the manual, and EVERY disagreement runs the same direction -- the manual says supported while the contract says developer, experimental, stub, deprecated, sample-extension or implementation-shim. That is the NORTH_STAR missing-plank signature: one fact wrong in two places at once. AREA51 is the canary: its own contract prose already said 'It read supported until 2026-08-30 while THIS PARAGRAPH already called it a developer probe.' The author caught it on one command; the systemic count is 33.
do_not_confuse_with: dispatchable (registered and runs); complete (no further work planned)

short_definition: The WORKING relational surface: SQLSEL (SELECT <list> FROM <table> [WHERE] [LIMIT], sqlsel_statement.cpp), SQL (COUNT with FOR <expr>, cmd_sql.cpp) and REL (relations dispatcher, cmd_rel.cpp). Distinct from the legacy reference catalogue.
student_note: SQLSEL is where real SELECT queries live.
user_note: SQLHELP is a reference catalogue, not the query engine.
developer_note: PROPOSED 2026-09-02, awaiting owner ruling on which name is canonical. Owner 2026-09-02: 'I have a generic sql help system for reference only before i had workspaces, now we really do have sql.' MEASURED: cmd_sql_help.cpp declares category: reference, status: experimental, and predates workspaces; sqlsel_statement.cpp carries lane AIF-074 and implements the P3 slice-1 grammar. The manual publishes SQL, SQLHELP, SQLSEL, SQLITE, SQLVER and SQLERASE as six peer entries, all marked supported, with nothing telling a reader which is the working system.
do_not_confuse_with: SQLHELP (reference catalogue only); SQLITE (embedded engine bridge); the SQL command (COUNT/FOR, not a SELECT engine)

short_definition: HOW AN AI AGENT REACHED THIS REPOSITORY when it produced a report: local_write | local_read_only | hosted_proposal | external_patch | human_operated_tool | automation.
developer_note: Controlled vocabulary, six values, declared in labtalk/registries/ai_report_audit.yaml under allowed_access_modes and enforced by labtalk/ai_portal/audit_trail.py. A value outside the six is an ADVISORY finding, not a seventh mode -- the correct response is to pick the registered term, never to widen the list. hosted_proposal covers a hosted model with NO repository access proposing a design package; local_read_only covers an agent that can read the tree but must not write. Measured 2026-09-02: one July manifest wrote the invented synonym 'remote' and printed an advisory on every commit for five weeks until it was corrected to hosted_proposal.
do_not_confuse_with: remote (never registered; an invented synonym for hosted_proposal); repository role (WHERE a tree sits, not HOW an agent reached it)
